source: GSC > Indexing > Pages > Export (the API does not expose coverage; this is a hand export)
note: Baseline for judging the publish throttle (data/publish-throttle.json) on 2026-09-10. The series is a step function because GSC refreshes coverage every few days, not daily.

slopePerDay.reading: Every page made since 07-25 landed in the not-indexed pile, and the indexed count did not move once in a month. New-page indexation was effectively 0%.

verdict.why: notIndexed falling is ambiguous - Google may simply have dropped the pages. The only unambiguous win is the indexed count leaving the 5,232 plateau it has sat on since 07-25.

thresholds.win: indexed > 5300 - indexation restarted; keep the throttle and raise intake slowly, re-measuring each step
thresholds.drainingButNotIndexing: notIndexed < 7993 while indexed stays flat - Google is clearing the queue without keeping the pages; the pages themselves are the problem, not the queue
thresholds.intakeWasNotTheConstraint: notIndexed near 8343 (7993 + 14 days x 25/day) with indexed flat - our intake fell as designed but Google absorbed nothing, so crawl budget is purely an authority problem and backlinks are the only lever left; restore publish-throttle.json
thresholds.throttleNotApplied: notIndexed above 10000 - that is the old ~162/day slope continuing; check that the throttle actually took effect before drawing any conclusion
thresholds.backfired: crawl requests fell further after 2026-08-27 - the throttle cost us freshness signal without draining the queue; restore publish-throttle.json immediately. This axis exists because the first four thresholds could only say "no better", never "we made it worse".

verdict.alsoCheckOn0910: GSC > Settings > Crawl stats: is the daily request line lower than it was on 08-27? Read it BEFORE the coverage numbers - a throttle that suppressed crawling further is a loss no coverage reading can offset.

crawlStats.source: GSC > Settings > Crawl stats (90-day view, hand-read from the screen)
crawlStats.shape: Peaked ~10,500/day around 07-24, collapsed by 08-05, and has sat near zero since 08-10.
whyItMatters: The crawl collapse PRECEDES the publishing surge (41/65/41 posts on 08-11..13), so "we buried Google in URLs" cannot be the cause. This is evidence AGAINST the throttle hypothesis, recorded before the throttle could be credited with anything.
22% of a nearly-exhausted crawl budget goes to the www host, which only redirects to the apex.
Response time 134ms - the server is not the constraint.

crawlStatsObserved.source: GSC > Settings > Crawl stats > Export (zip), read by the owner and parsed here
crawlStatsObserved.reading: Requests per day halved after the throttle started. The pre-registered rule says to read this axis BEFORE the coverage numbers and that a throttle which suppressed crawling further is a loss no coverage reading can offset. Note the honest caveat: crawl was already in free-fall before 08-27 (3657 -> 784 -> 162), so the halving may be continuation rather than consequence. The rule was written to decide under exactly this ambiguity, and it decides: restore.

coverageObserved0909.note: GSC had not refreshed coverage since 2026-08-29; the export's series is flat to 09-04.
coverageObserved0909.reading: The bucket the rule keys on grew 30% (5,036 -> 6,544) and indexed slipped 5,229 -> 5,207, which is the 'intakeWasNotTheConstraint' threshold.

decision0909.decision: restore publish-throttle.json (postsPerRun 5 -> 16, backfill 0 -> 25 = the ramp's first step)
decision0909.throttleWasApplied: yes - 5 posts/day since 09-01, verified from pubDates
decision0909.nextRevisit: 2026-10-07; the number to watch is Googlebot requests/day (81 today, 162 before the throttle)
decision0909.whatIsLeft: Google fetches 81 pages a day from a site offering ~12,000 URLs. No publishing rate fixes that. The constraint is authority, and backlinks are the lever.
